motion.name: tile-lift

motion.name: radar-sweep
motion.value: conic mask --sweep 0deg to 360deg, 1.8s ease-out-expo, 0.25s delay; beam fades 0.6s at 1.6s
motion.purpose: The one authored moment on the Couplet shot; gated by :root:not([data-swept]).

motion.name: bridge-exchange
motion.value: msg-in 520ms, packet 650ms, each delayed 1300ms + step offset
motion.purpose: dmcl Bridge exchange, plays once after the sweep; same data-swept gate.

motion.name: route-transition
motion.value: old root fade 160ms ease-out; new root rise 8px 420ms; shared groups 520ms
motion.purpose: View-transition route changes; shot-<slug> names morph shared screenshots.

motion.name: theme-reveal
motion.value: clip-path circle from the toggle, 550ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Theme switch through a view transition; instant under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All motion off under prefers-reduced-motion; content visible by default.

narrative.overview:
A green-black ground with tiles set one step up, each tile holding a real thing that works: the Couplet radar, the Temperature Alarms dashboard, a labelled illustration of the dmcl chat bridge. Tile size follows importance, never equality. The page shows; it does not describe. Copy is short, set in Mona Sans at a slightly widened stretch for headings, and the only chromatic voice is one leaf green that means "live, shipped, focused".

Density is calm and confident: a 1200px container, 12px gutters between tiles, generous 24 to 28px inner padding, hairline borders instead of heavy shadows. Motion is exponential ease-out throughout, with exactly one authored moment per session (the radar sweep and the bridge exchange) and everything visible by default. The world follows the system theme; light mode is a green-tinted paper version of the same structure, not a different design.

Confirmed rejections: the "Hi, I'm X" hero over a row of equal cards, neon glow, stack pills, invented claims, and stock or mocked-up imagery standing in for real work.
keyCharacteristics: Bento grid at 12 columns; the flagship spans 7 columns by 2 rows.
Real screenshots set flush into the tile's bottom-right corner.
One accent (leaf) plus one status companion (bud); everything else is green-tinted neutral.
Mona Sans Variable for everything; width (font-stretch) and weight carry the hierarchy.
Hairline borders and tonal steps for depth; shadows barely exist.
One authored load moment per session, all motion off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Leaf Rule
rules.body: Leaf green is the only accent. It means live, shipped, or focused; it is never used as decoration, a gradient fill, or a heading color.

rules.name: The Paired Token Rule
rules.body: Every color is defined once as a light-dark() pair on :root. Never add a theme-specific override block; data-theme only pins color-scheme.

rules.name: The Third-Party Palette Rule
rules.body: Hard-coded Minecraft and Discord colors live only inside the Bridge illustration, where they mimic those products. They are not part of this palette.

rules.name: The Stretch-Not-Shout Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from width, weight, and negative tracking within Mona Sans. Do not introduce a second display face.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No small uppercase kicker above headings. A heading stands on its own; context goes in the status line beneath it.

rules.name: The Importance-Sized Rule
rules.body: A tile's span follows the project's weight. Never lay out a row of equal cards for unequal work.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No colored box-shadows, text glows, or neon halos. The only light effects are the static, low-alpha canopy wash behind the home hero (home only, masked out by 720px) and the transient radar beam during the one-time sweep.

rules.name: The Flush Bleed Rule
rules.body: A screenshot that bleeds to a tile's edge cancels the tile's padding on those sides and drops its own radius on the bleeding corners, so the tile's 20px corner clips it. It keeps its 12px top-left corner and strong hairline where it sits inside the tile.

dos: Do define every color once as a light-dark() pair and let the system theme decide; data-theme only pins it.
Do put the real artifact in the tile: an actual screenshot of the shipped product, framed at 12px and bled flush to the tile edge.
Do label anything that is not a literal screenshot with a note badge and an aria-label that says it is an illustration.
Do size tiles by importance on the 12-column grid with 12px gaps.
Do use the status line (dot plus "Status · Year") under every project name.
Do keep one authored motion moment per session, gated by data-swept, and switch all motion off under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do give shared imagery a shot-<slug> view-transition name so it morphs between routes.
donts: Don't add eyebrows or uppercase kickers above headings.
Don't render tech stacks as pills or badges; the stack is one muted line of names joined by " · ".
Don't use glow: no colored shadows, neon halos, or text glow.
Don't use stock imagery, mockups, or fabricated screenshots; if there is no real visual, the tile stays text-only.
Don't introduce a second accent; bud is a status color only.
Don't add a second display face or system display fallback as a design choice; Mona Sans carries every role.
Don't lay out equal cards for unequal work.
